text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty -> page: SEV-2 / region-network-high-latency (eu-west-1). Incident created: 1789054321

oncall-sre: seeing increased 5xx and TCP retransmits from eu-west-1. Dashboards show ELB target health dropping in az-1d. Paging oncall.

tilly: I see spike in backend error rate ~ 07:12 UTC, ELB (app/redwood-api-euw1) target group showing unhealthy in az-d only. Other AZs OK.

raj: Route53 latency also rising for eu-west-1 endpoints, some Route53 healthchecks failing. Might be control-plane flapping?

maria: customers reporting elevated error rates for hosted API in eu-west-1 — ticket volume increasing. Customer-ops tracking.

incident-bot: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/az-network-deg (follow AZ-network-deg -> failover-to-secondary-region)

dan: quick triage: EC2 / ENI attachments in az-1d show errors provisioning new ENIs, NATGW in az-1d showing "Pending" for some time. Possible AZ-level networking provisioning issue on AWS.

oncall-sre: confirmed ENI failures in az-1d across multiple instance types. EBS attachments appear fine. Notifying AWS support, opening a high-priority case.

raj: starting customer impact assessment: which customers have primary Dedicated or Private workloads pinned to eu-west-1/az-1d? List incoming — looks like 6 Dedicated pools, 12 customer Private nodes.

maria: temp comms: "We're investigating increased errors in eu-west-1. We're routing around affected AZ, will provide updates every 15m." posting to status.redwood.ai incident page. :loudspeaker:

dan: mitigation plan option 1: reweight Route53 to shift ~100% traffic away from eu-west-1 -> eu-west-3 (if customers allow inter-region). Option 2: create NLBs in healthy AZs and update target groups / ELB config to avoid az-1d.

oncall-sre: starting controlled traffic shift to bypass az-1d. Lowering Route53 TTL to 30s via change batch to speed convergence.

# command
oncall-sre: ran:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z0123456789 --change-batch file://shift-euw1-away.json
```
file contains weighted records: eu-west-3 weight=100, eu-west-1 weight=0 for api.redwood.ai

tilly: also adding health-check override to mark az-1d endpoints unhealthy to accelerate failover.

incident-bot: NOTE: lowering TTL for api endpoints to 30s may increase cache churn and billing. Confirm?

oncall-sre: acknowledged, proceed. Customer impact priority > cost.

maria: Customer-ops: proactively reaching out to top-10 customers in eu-west-1 with Dedicated stacks, advising short-lived degradation and asking permission to fail traffic to eu-west-3. Two customers requested we keep them in eu-west-1; logged a follow-up with account.

raj: AWS support responded: seeing "ENI assignment and NAT gateway provisioning delays" in eu-west-1/az-1d. They've escalated to internal networking team. No ETA yet.

dan: created temporary NLBs in eu-west-1 az-a/b and attached healthy targets, updated ELB routing policies to avoid az-1d. This reduced 5xx by ~60% within 3 minutes.

tilly: monitoring metrics: p95 latency back to baseline for most routes, error rate still elevated for a subset pinned to az-1d (private + dedicated pinned instances).

incident-bot: Handoff reminder -> scheduled oncall rotation at 07:45 UTC. Current oncall to provide warm handoff to next oncall.

oncall-sre: @tilly please take the handoff, I'll escalate with AWS and continue the runbook for pinned Dedicated pools. Summary: traffic shifted, temporary NLBs created, AWS investigating ENI/NATGW provisioning in az-1d, customer comms live.

tilly: taking handoff. Action items: 1) keep Route53 weight change until AWS confirms AZ healthy, 2) replace pinned Dedicated instances in az-1d with replacements in other AZs where feasible, 3) prepare rollback plan if we see route flapping.

maria: posting update to status page and emailing impacted customers. Copy of comms: "We have shifted traffic away from one availability zone in eu-west-1 to reduce errors. We're working with AWS to restore full capacity; you may see increased latency as traffic reroutes."

raj: started automation to replace pinned Dedicated instances: running script to spin up new VMs in eu-west-1 az-a then migrate workloads, sample command:
```
./scripts/replace-dedicated -c eu-west-1 -from az-1d -to az-1a -pool redwood-ded-42
```
Estimated per-pool migration ~ 8-12 min.

incident-bot: AWS support updated case: internal remediation in progress, they will attempt to "reconcile ENI allocations" and clear NATGW backlog. No ETA, next update in 30m.

tilly: replaced 4 of 6 Dedicated pools; error rate for those customers normalized. Two remaining customers are manually approved to keep traffic in-eu-west-1 until after business hours — tracking as exceptions.

oncall-sre: continuing watch. Please escalate to SRE-lead if AWS ETA > 60m or if error rates rise again.

maria: compiling incident timeline and affected-customer list for postmortem. Will attach logs and routing diffs.

dan: note for post-incident: consider automatic relocation of pinned Dedicated nodes when AZ provisioning issues detected (runbook enhancement).

incident-bot: Update 07:55 UTC: partial recovery observed; AWS reports "progress" in reconciliation. We'll keep Route53 weights and temporary NLBs for at least 60m to ensure stability.

tilly: marking incident as mitigated for public-facing traffic. Still investigating pinned/private workload residuals.

maria: next update to customers and status page scheduled in 30m.

oncall-sre: handing off active watch to tilly at 07:45 UTC. If anything spikes, page oncall immediately and follow runbook az-network-deg.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated (partial). Case: AWS-123456789. Thread will continue for postmortem notes.
